A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SubspaceAD by the same authors. All 14 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables and supplementary material, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original SubspaceAD experiments on MVTec-AD and VisA, including few-shot, batched zero-shot, full-shot, ablation and timing results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations, updates their results and adds scoring-head timing and rotation-preprocessing experiments.

M1.justification: The documented DINOv2 feature averaging, PCA subspace fitting, reconstruction-residual scoring and TVaR aggregation remain unchanged. Explicitly describing PCA as deterministic clarifies the existing procedure; the revised use of scores for metrics concerns evaluation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same MVTec-AD and VisA categories and anomaly detection/localization tasks under few-shot, batched zero-shot and full-shot settings. The new Transistor ablation changes support-image augmentation within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained in the matched accuracy, qualitative, full-shot and end-to-end timing comparisons. The new scoring-head timing analysis reuses AnomalyDINO; removing citations from Table 1 does not remove any baseline.

E3.justification: Section 3.4 changes the stated AUROC/PRO input from normalized maps to raw scores, revising a central evaluation procedure without establishing whether earlier experiments were rerun. v2 also introduces same-H100 scoring-head timing controls and a Transistor protocol with rotated support images. Main benchmark resolution remains 672 pixels.

E4.justification: New Appendix G tests the effect of rotation augmentation on the orientation-sensitive Transistor category. Expanded Appendix D isolates scoring overhead and examines its dependence on shot count. These are targeted additions to the retained design ablations and qualitative failure analyses.

E5.justification: v1 describes averaging over sampled support images without specifying run counts or reporting uncertainty. v2 specifies five independent seeds and adds mean ± standard deviation to the main and per-category results and the new rotation ablation. This substantially expands statistical reporting, but does not establish an increase from a known earlier run count.

E6.justification: Main, per-category and ablation results are extensively revised. Table 1's one-shot MVTec-AD image AUROC changes from 98.0 to 97.1 ± 0.9; Table 2's batched zero-shot VisA AUROC changes from 97.7 to 94.1, tying MuSc. Four-shot VisA PRO changes from 94.1 to 93.8, below AnomalyDINO's 94.1. New timing and rotation results are added. These are revised reports, not established same-setting algorithmic gains or losses.

T1.justification: The subspace assumption, probabilistic model, variance threshold, projection, residual and aggregation equations retain their mathematical substance. Equation renumbering and the deterministic-PCA clarification introduce no new theorem, proof or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contribution: training-free DINOv2-plus-PCA anomaly detection without memory banks or prompt tuning, with state-of-the-art few-shot performance. Updated headline numbers do not redefine that contribution or its stated scope.

C2.justification: Appendix D replaces its cross-GPU speed-superiority argument with an explicit comparability warning and a finding of similar scoring-head latency. Section 4.7 emphasizes resolution saturation and encoder-dependent deployment constraints. Appendix G explains how rotation augmentation can make rotational defects appear normal. Existing logical-anomaly and background-clutter limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly identifies deterministic PCA, clarifies the common 672-pixel resolution and documents scoring-head measurements after feature extraction on an H100. The '(w/ Reg)' backbone qualifier disappears without an explicit statement of an architectural change. Code and demo access information remains equivalent.

R1.justification: v2 adds a Wikipedia PCA reference to credit the illustration in Figure 2. A duplicate PatchCore bibliography entry is removed while the underlying work remains cited. Related-work coverage and research positioning otherwise remain stable.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites affect implementation, performance and ablation discussions, and Appendix D gains separate latency subsections. Appendix G is added, alongside small notation and reference cleanups. The overall narrative and main section order are retained.

P2.justification: Figures 4–5 are redrawn with revised axes, legends and styling; Figure 5 is repositioned. Tables 1, 5 and 6 accommodate uncertainty values, and new Tables 9 and 11 present timing and rotation results. The original timing table becomes Table 10. Qualitative illustrations remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Five-seed uncertainty reporting and the same-GPU scoring-head comparison address v1's unspecified variability and misleading cross-GPU speed argument; Appendix G also tests the preprocessing exception. These improve empirical transparency. The gain is limited by incomplete reconciliation: Figure 4's revised legend contradicts its caption, and Appendix B still claims DINOv3 is consistently worse despite Table 7 versus the updated Table 1.
